Rumbling and fermentation. Colic and
backache at same time. Much flatus: cholera infantum.

sections.text:
Urine scanty, slimy, flaky, sandy, bloody.
Gravel. Renal colic. Severe pain at conclusion of
urination. Urine dribbles while sitting. Bladder dis-
tended and tender. Child screams before and while
passing urine. Sand on diaper. Renal colic and dysuria
in infants. Pain from right kidney downward. Tenes-
mus of bladder; urine passes in thin, feeble stream.
Pain at meatus.

Bloody, seminal emissions. Intolerable stench
on genitals. Herpetic eruption on genitals. Itching on
scrotum and perineum. Syphilis; squamous eruption
and bone pains.

(twelfth day), 16 .—Frequent stitches on vertex, 3 .— Varietals. Pressing in
left side of head, particularly in the temple, during rest and motion, 2 .—
Sensation as if screwed together in both sides of the head, half an hour
after breakfast (sixth day), 6 .—A pressure-like tearing in the whole left
side of head, 2 . —[100.] Pressing and itching deep in the right half of
head, morning (eighth day), 6 .— Pressing, with frequent stitches, in left side
of head, moruihg (ninth day), 6 .—Beating and sounding in the right side
of head, deep in the brain, forenoon (ninth day), 6 .—Violent throbbing in
right side of head, deep in brain, 6 .—Violent pressing-tearing stitches in
right side of head, so that he shudders, 2 .—Frequent stitches in side of
head, 6 .—Dull stinging in left side of head, to the nape of the neck, 1 .—
Stinging drawing on right parietal and temporal bone, 3 .—Stinging tearing
on parietal bone in left vertex, 3 .— Occiput. Stinging pain in left occi¬
put, 2 .—[HO.] Twitching on left side of occiput, 6 .— External Head.
Falling off of the hair, with great sensitiveness of the scalp on combing
(sixth day), 6 .—External headache, like compressions and incisions, 1 .—
Pulsating stitches on the forehead, 1 .—Frequent itching on the whole head,
does not cease after scratching (eighth day), 6 .—Itchiug on scalp, disap¬
pearing after scratching (sixth day), 6 .—Scalp, fine pricking itching, 2 .—


529

Itching in right half of head, 6 .—Itching on posterior part of scalp, 1 .—
Severe pressure and stitches on vertex, towards right side, 3 .

Eye.— [120.] B ruised pain in right eye on turning eyes to left (six¬
teenth day), 16 .—Pain of the eyes when he looks at anything in the daylight, 1 .
—Pressure in left eye, as from a grain of sand, 6 .—Pressure in the left, then
in the right eye, with dimness of vision, 6 .—Pressing in eyes alternates with
burning, 1 .—Stinging frequent in both eyes, as if dust or sand were in them;
outdoors it seems better, 6 .—Stinging in the eyes on closing the lids, and
violent pain when the closed eyes are pressed upon ; at the same time, a
broad red stripe extending from cornea to the older canihus; the inner corners
are turned blue, and the right is somewhat swollen (twenty-first day), 6 .—
On closing eyes stinging in them, 6 .—Reading by candlelight hurts eyes,
paper looks red, 1 .—In the morning all objects affect the eyes, 1 .— Lids.
[130.] Inflamed dry eyelids, 1 .—Violent burning and agglutination of the
eyelids, on awaking in the morning, 6 .—Quivering in right upper eyelid, 1 .—
Burning in the eyelids constantly, sometimes alternating with pressing pain
in the same , 1 .—Lachrynidi Apparatus. Lachrymatiou of the eyes
in the daytime; in the morning they are agglutinated (fourth day), 6 .—
Lachrymatiou of the eyes, every other day (sixth day), 6 .—Tears in eyes
when gaping,®— JPlipil. Pupils dilated (in two hours), 4 .— Lull. Press¬
ing in ball of the eye, evenings, while reading by candlelight, with red
shine of paper, 1 .— Vision. Flickering before eyes, and headache, 1 . —
[140.] Mist before the eyes and dulness, 7 .—Great dimness of left eye, as if
a gauze were spread over it, afternoon (sixth day), 6 .—Dimness of vision,
as in a fog [first day), 6 .—Dimness of vision, 6 .—Blackness and headache, 1 .

Ear. — Inflammation and swelling of a gland under the right ear,
which begins to suppurate on sixth day, 6 .—Drawing and visible twitching
in the lobule of left ear, later either in the right or left, 6 .—Painful con¬
striction about external right ear, 2 .—Stinging beneath and in front of left
ear, as with a bristle, in the morning (sixth day), 6 .—Tearing upwards be¬
hind left ear. frequently in the atternoon, 6 .— [150.] In the ear violent
pressure and compression, up into the temple, where it also presses, 2 .—
Tearing in right ear, mornings (fourth day), 6 .—Tearing pressure in right
cartilage and external meatus of ear, 3 .—Contracting sensation in right
ear, 2 .—Ulcerative pain deep in left ear and around the anterior part of the
same, morning (sixth day), 6 .—Violent dull stitches, deep in right ear, fore¬
noon (ninth day), 6 .—Tolling of bells in left ear, for some time, afternoon
(sixth day), 6 .—Ringing in left ear, 2 .—Every word reverberates in his head,
cannot speak, with headache, 1 .

sections.label: Nose
sections.text:
Coryza, especially on right side (tenth day), 15 .— [160.] Coryza
and cough, 1 .—Stuffed coryza, without sneezing, no air passes through the
nose, 1 .—Very thick mucus from the nose, 6 .—Frequent nosebleed (sixth
day); at night, after dream of fighting, 6 .—Epistaxis, with feeling as if
small bubbles were bursting in the nose (third day), 6 .—In the evening,
bleeding from right nostril when blowing nose, light-colored blood (fourth
day), 15 .—Bleeding from left nostril while blowing nose (eleventh day), 15 .—
Bleeding from right nostril, 1 .—Nosebleed, 0 .—Sneezing in the morning, after
rising, 6 .— [170.] Sneezing, fails in the attempt (eighth day), 6 .—Sneezing
and running coryza, only in the morning (second day), 6 .—Stoppage of the
nose in the forenoon, a short time, 6 .—Stoppage of nose and gloomy mood, 7 .
—Woke with dry obstruction of right nostril (sixth day), 15 .—Burning in
the nose, on blowing it, 6 .—In the nose burning on blowing it, with a dry
cough, 6 .—In the tip of the nose, pricking as if caused by a needle, 1 .

VOL. VIII.—34

530

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Twitching of right side of upper lip (after three hours and a
half), 15 .—Violent pain in the face, as if bruised, about both inferior orbital
margins, on waking in the morning, but only on pressure (twenty-first
day), 6 .— [180.] Drawing, stinging, tearing in the masticatory muscles of
right side, which seem to have spasmodically contracted, 2 .—Pressing-sting¬
ing pain on lower inner edge of right lower jaw, but only on touch, and on
bending the head back, 3 .—Stiffness and tension in masseter muscles and
joints of the jaw, on moving the part, thirty minutes, forenoon (sixth day), 6 .
—The jaws pain as if they would break, 1 .

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Teeth. Chattering of teeth, with chill, 6 .—Toothache on the
right side, with creeping, crawling, tingling in the roots of the teeth ; after
picking them until they bleed, the pain, which had been much more severe
for awhile, ceases, evening (thirteenth and fourteenth days), 6 .—Drawing
toothache in the right lower row, with heaviness of the head, particularly
on the right side, from 4 a.m. till evening (third day), 6 .—The right upper
teeth are very sensitive on biting on them (fourteenth and fifteenth days), 6 .
—Tearing in the teeth from cold draft of air or cold drink, 7 .—Molars of
left side and one on the right begin to ache, 6 . — [190.] Toothache, on two
successive evenings (eighth day), 6 .—Stinging in a tooth which had been
painful for a long time, forenoon (ninth day), 6 .— Gums. Swelling and
sore pain of the gums of the inner side of lower maxilla, 1 .—The gums of
the left lower row are painful on smoking tobacco, afternoon (third day), 6 .
—Stinging tearing in the gums and the root of the last right lower molar, 3 .
—Tearing in the gums of the right lower row, in the evening (fourth
day), 6 .— Tongue. Whitish coating on the tongue, in the morning, with
natural taste (third day), 6 .—Aphthae on the tongue and palate (seventeenth
day), 7 .—Tongue is rough several mornings on waking, passing off after
eating, 6 .—Stitches in the tongue, 1 .— General Mouth. [200.] Offensive
breath, 1 .—Slimy mouth in the morning (sixth day), 6 .—Dry mouth, after
stool, at 3.30 a.m. (seventh day), 16 .—Dryness in the mouth, without thirst,
forenoon, 6 .—Dryness in mouth and throat, mornings in bed (seventh day), 6 .
—Woke with dry mouth (twenty-second day), 16 .—Pressing-drawing pain
in soft palate, 3 .— Saliva. Frequently tasteless water collects in the mouth,
forenoon, till 1 p.m. (second day), 6 .—Salivation, 20 .— Taste. Woke with
fishy disagreeable taste in mouth (sixth day), 13 .—[210.] Metallic taste for
two days, 7 .—Sweetish taste in the mouth, while smoking tobacco, 6 —In¬
sipid sweetish taste, 7 .—Taste in throat is always sweetish, like liquorice,
several days, 6 .—Herbaceous taste in mouth, 1 .—Nauseous herbaceous taste
in the mouth , 1 .—*Bitter taste in the mouth, in the morning, after rising, soon
abating,' 1 .—Bitter taste on the under lip, mornings (eighth day), 6 .—Bitter
taste of rye bread, 4 .—Disagreeable, very sour, and slimy taste in the fauces,
mornings, like sour dough (leaven), 1 .

Throat— [220.] Constant hawking of mucus in the morning; the
mucus is constantly reproduced in abundance (second day), 6 .—Phlegm in
throat all day, which she could not detach or swallow (tenth day), 15 .—
Tough mucus in throat, mornings; cannot be removed by hawking, for sev¬
eral days, 6 .—Mucus in throat tastes like blood (eleventh day), 15 .—Hoarse¬
ness in the throat, every other day (after six days), 6 .—Hoarseness in the
throat frequently returning (after three hours), 6 .—Constricting feeling in
the throat and chest, with difficult breathing, frequently in the day (fifth
day), 6 .—Spasmodic constriction in the throat; he is forced to loosen his
clothes, the cravat, the shirt, in order to get sufficient breath, but without
avail (sixth day), 6 .—Sensation of constriction in the posterior portion of


531

the throat, 11 .—Irritation and constriction in the throat, 11 .— [230.] Rough¬
ness in the throat excites cough, 6 .—Rough, hoarse, and dry in the throat,
in the morning, on awaking, tor a quarter of an hour, 6 .—During cough,
roughness in the throat, mornings (second day), 6 .—Dryness in the throat
and stinging on swallowing, morning (seventh day), 6 .—Spasmodic urging
or straining in the throat through the whole night, but frequently vomit¬
ing, 6 .—Wheu swallowing, a pain in the throat; a feeling of rawness on the
larynx, a pressing sensation moving about in larynx, with a cough at night
and in the morning, with a colorless tasteless expectoration ; when he
coughs the larynx pains most, 10 *.—Pain in right side of throat, as if caused
by a sharp spelt of barley or wheat, up along at the side and out at the
ear, only passing off in the afternoon, after lying down (first day), 6 .—Irri¬
tation in the posterior portion of the throat, 11 .—Stinging from throat out
of ear, 6 .—In fauces tickliug ulcerative sensation, causing a cough, 1 .— [240.]
In the morning very much burning in the oesophagus (fourth day), 15 .—In
the swallow acrid sensation, 8 .—Throat swollen, with falling down uncon¬
scious, 1 . — At 10.30 A.M., transient tensive feeling (not pain) in region of
right submaxillary gland (thirteenth day), 16 .

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Appetite and Thirst. More appetite than usual,
for several days, 6 .—He longs for his dinner, with an ardent desire, 9 .—(Wants
nothing but juicy fruits), 10a .—Gnawing hungry sensation, 21 .—No appetite
for smoking tobacco, the taste of which seems to him to be entirely changed
(fifth, sixth, and seventh days), 6 .—All his appetite is gone, 10 *.— [ 250 .] No
appetite for breakfast (sixth day), 6 .—No appetite and no hunger ; food had
not enough flavor, and after a meal it seemed to him as if he had eaten
nothing; as if the stomach were without sensation, 1 .—No hunger or appe¬
tite; he ate but little at noon (second day), 6 .—Loathing at the thought of
the food eaten, 1 .—Ability to go about all day fasting, 12 .—Thirst, even in the
morning, continuing all day, with general warmth (third day), 6 .—Thirst,
frequently throughout the day, with one who is usually not thirsty, 6 .—
Thirst for water, in the afternoon, 2 o’clock, after chill before dinner (first
day), 6 .—Absence of thirst during meals, contrary to bis habit (first to fourth
day), 6 . — Entire absence of thirst during the whole proving, 6 . — Eructa¬
tions. [ 260 .] First bitter and sour then eaipty eructations, 6 .—Sour eruc¬
tations before and after attack, 1 .—Continual eructation, with shuddering, 6 .
—Eructation, with taste of the food, after dinner (fifth day), 6 .—Bitter eruc¬
tation in the morning, after rising, with bitter taste in the mouth (second
day), 6 .—Bitter eructation during dinner; ceases after the meal (second
day), 6 .—After eating the usual wassersoup, and drinking a little cold water
after it, the soup eructated with a bitter taste (fourth day), 6 .—Belching up
of bitter sour matter, evenings; he had to spit it out three times, 6 .—Belch¬
ing of sour water, afternoon, 6 .—Continuous sour eructation, 1 .— [ 270 .] Fre¬
quent empty eructation, forenoon and evening; evening (second day), and
forenoon (fifth day), 6 .—Belching of bitter water, before and once after din¬
ner (fourth day), 6 .—Sour eructation after breakfast, 1 .—Constant imperfect
eructations, 2 .—Ineffectual inclination to eruct, with spasmodic twisting in
stomach, immediately after dinner, lasting one minute, 6 .— Hiccough.
Hiccough after dinner, three spells (second day), 6 .—Hiccough, 6 p.m., for
a long while, 6 . — Hiccoughing eructation (soon), 6 . —Nausea and Vom¬
iting. Constant nausea, without inclination to vomit, afternoon (third
day), 6 .—Nausea, 19 .— [ 280 .] Nausea, with an acrid sensation on the tongue
and in the swallow, 8 .—It has nauseating effects, 18 .—Much nausea, with
constant ineffectual inclination to vomit, the whole forenoon (first day), 6 .

532


—Severe nausea, mornings, increased to vomiting, with increased herba¬
ceous taste in the mouth, 1 .—Nausea after breakfast, 1 .—Nausea, with ver¬
tigo, 6 .—Nausea, with headache, 1 .—Nausea, with constriction of the stom¬
ach, 6 .—Nausea and exhaustion after dinner, 1 .—Nausea in the throat, caused
by the rising of a nauseous vapor into the mouth, with affection of the
head, 1 .— [290.] Nausea and inclination to vomit; it comes up constantly
(third day), 6 .—Constant inclination to vomit, 10 ®.—Efforts to vomit, 11 .—She
has to vomit often, and each time her nose bleeds, 10 ®.—Vomiting of bitter
substances with great efforts, 11 .—He said it made him as sick as death and
broke all his bones, 19 .—Sick stomach and prostration, kind of coryza, had
to lie down, and could not move; pulse somewhat retarded, 8 .—Vomits her
breakfast after pain in the stomach, 10 ®.—Sour vomiting, 5 ; with headache, 1 .
— Stomach. If he eats ever so little, it nevertheless distends his stomach
as much as if he had eaten a great deal, 1 .— [300.] During menses griping
in pit of stomach, extending toward the sacrum, 1 .—Griping in pit of stom¬
ach, extending toward the sacrum, 1 .—Spasmodic twisting in stomach, 6 .—
Often spasmodic sensation in pit of stomach, 1 .—Constriction in the stom¬
ach, with nausea, vanishing at night (ninth day), 6 .—Pressure in pit of stom¬
ach, evening, while singing (fourth day), 6 .—Pressing pain in epigastrium
and directly under the ensiform cartilage, increased by touch, 3 .—Pressure
in stomach, with soft stool, 7 .—Sense of weakness in the stomach, 11 .—It is very
subject to lie heavy on the stomach and to produce indigestion/ 2 .— [310. J
Heat and burning in the stomach (soon), 6 .—Heat in the stomach, as after
spirituous beverages, after eating a mouthful of bread (sixth day), 6 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Hypochondria. Stinging in left hypochondriac re¬
gion, particularly on bending toward the right; continuing a long time, fore¬
noon (first day), 6 .—Dull pressure in the region of the liver; she often had
returns of it; felt only in the morning on waking; better after getting up
and walking about; after Sepia high,it disappeared for ten or twelve days, 10 ®.
— The left hypochondriac region pains as if bruised, with throbbing, 1 p.m., 6 .
— Umbilicus and Sides. Cutting around the navel, always on gap-
ing (eighth day), 6 .—Cutting in a small spot about the navel, morning (eighth
day), 6 .—Cutting around the navel, then moving about in the abdomen, dis¬
appearing after passage of flatus, forenoon (eighth day), 6 .—Painful pressure
inwards and pinching in left side of abdomen, in small spot, aggravated
only by deep inspiration, 2 .—Pressing pain in left side of abdomen, 1 .—
[ 320 .] Cutting pain on a narrow line of the left side of the abdomen,
transversely towards the back ; then rolling in the belly and disappear¬
ance of the pain (sixth day), 6 .—Stinging, now in the right, now in the left
side of abdomen (seventh day), 6 .—Severe stinging under the right ribs and
in abdomen, one hour after dinner (sixth day), 6 .—Stinging in the left side
of abdomen (soon), 1 .—Stinging in left side of abdomen, in the morning,
while sitting; vanishing while walking, 6 .— General Abdomen. Great
fulness in abdomen, after eating or drinking anything, 6 .—Distension of ab¬
domen (sixth day), 6 .—Frequent discharge of flatus all day (after eight
days), 6 .—Flatulency, with dulness in the head, 1 .—Discharge of offensive
flatus, 1 .— [ 330 .] Discharge of flatus of fetid odor, evenings (third day), 6 .
—Discharge of flatus upwards and downwards, 1 .— Rambling in abdomen,
with feeling of emptiness in the same, 6 . —Rumbling and rolling in abdomen,
every day, without diarrhoea and without distension, 1 .—Rolling in the belly
and fermentation, 6 .—Rumbling and clucking in abdomen, with feeling of
emptiness in the same, 2 .—Rumbling and growling in bowels, 6 .—Loud quack¬
ing in abdomen, as in spasms ; remitting for a while after eructation (twenty-


533

first and twenty-third days), 6 .—Abdomen very sensitive on pressure, 10
a.m., 6 . —During the diarrhoea rolling and fermentation in abdomen, with
discharge of stinking flatus (seventh day), 6 .— [340.] During menses fre¬
quent griping colic, 1 .—Colic, with diarrhoea, 6 .—Colicky abdominal pain in
the morning (second day), 6 .—Feels as if empty and disembowelled in ab¬
domen, soon after breakfast (eighth day), 6 .—Frequent spasmodic sensations
in abdomen, 1 .—Constriction of intestines, 1 .—Contracting pain of the bowels,
then violent rumbling and grumbling; now around the navel, now up¬
ward toward the chest, now again downward, as if diarrhoea were to fol¬
low, forenoon (second day), 6 .— Pinching and rolling in abdomen, from 5
p.m. till midnight, preventing sleep, 6 .—Pinching and rumbling in abdomen,
after eating; later passing upon left side towards the stomach, and only
dispelled by doubling up, 6 .—Pinching colic during menses, 1 .— [350.] Cutting
in abdomen, with scanty stool, 6 .—Violent cutting in abdomen, 5 p.m., then
semifluid diarrhoeic stools (sixth day), 6 .—Severe pinching in abdomen, 6 .—
Severe pinching in abdomen, and thereupon painful contraction of sphincter
ani,\—Pressing drawing in abdomen, as after cold, 3 .—Motion in the bowels,
with burning (soon), 6 .—Motion in abdomen, as before diarrhoea, all day, 6 .
— Feeling of inactivity of bowels, 1 .—Burning and beat in abdomen, 6 .—Cold¬
ness and motion in abdomen (ninth day), 6 .— [360.] Internal chilliness in
the abdomen, 1 .— Hypogastrium and Iliac Region. Straining
constriction in hypogastrium, vanishing after passage of flatus, evening and
forenoon (seventeenth and eighteenth days), 6 .—A moving and tossing about
in lower belly, as if he had taken a purgative, but without diarrhoea, the
whole day (after forty-eight hours), 6 .—Pinching in left inguinal region, 2 .—
In right groin severe tension, 1 .—On appearance of menses, soreness in the
bend of the right groin, and urging to urinate, 6 .—Slight soreness in right
groin (sixth day), 16 .—Soreness in the left groin, as the pain in the testicles
and spermatic cords got better (eighth day), 16 .

Rectum and Anas ,—Ulcer on the anus of the size of a walnut,
bearing a black pustule, soon opening with pain, and discharging pus, 1 .—
During the diarrhoeic stool sensation of corroding acridity in rectum, dur¬
ing the discharge, 1 .— [370.] Tearing and cutting in rectum, 1 .—Painful con¬
traction of sphincter ani, after pinching in abdomen, 2 .—Severe aching in
anus, with frequent desire for stool; better after stool, but went away very
slowly; it was relieved by hard pressure upwards in anus, at 3.30 a.m.
(seventh day), 16 . — Soreness in the anus, wakes him at night, and then
changes into a burning itching, lasting all day, 1 .—Burning in anus after
stool, after fluid stools, 6 .—Itching on the right side of anus, dispelled by
scratching (eighth day), 6 .—Tenesmus in anus after stool, 6 .—Uncontrollable
urgent desire; but nevertheless only scanty soft stool, passing with great
difficulty through the seemingly contracted rectum, 1 .—Urgent desire, with
contraction of intestines, and enormous pressure downwards, as if contents
of abdomen were to be pressed out, for several minutes ; then at last some¬
thing passes with a jerk, with severe tearing and cutting in rectum ; there¬
upon immediately again desire to go to stool, as if rectum were being
pressed out, so that he can scarcely sit on account of pain, 1 .—Frequent
urging to go to stool, with scanty discharge, and with tenesmus in the anus
afterwards (second day), 6 .— [380.] Stool accompanied with much urging
and straining in the rectum, 1 .—Desire, but no stool, 1 .

Stool, —Frequent diarrhoeic discharges, four or five times during the
day, with colic (fifth and sixth days), 6 .—Semifluid diarrhoeic stools, 6 .—■
Twice diarrhoea (fourth day), 7 .—Hurried action of bowels before break-

534


fast, 14 .—Stool was semifluid toward the end (ninth day), 6 .—Very soft stool,
without any other complaint (second day), 6 .—Fluid stools, evenings, with
burning in anus afterwards, 6 .—Soft stool, with tenesmus in anus after
it (second day), 6 .— [390.] Stool softer than usual, accompanied with slight
pressure in region of stomach, 7 .—Scanty consistent stool, accompanied by
cutting in the abdomen, 6 .—Pitchy, sticky, adhesive stool several days, 6 .
Stool, the first part of which was hard, the last soft, with subsequent burn¬
ing in the anus, 6 .—Scanty stool, preceded by evacuation of much flatus, at
3.30 a.m. (seventh day) ; had had a natural stool the day before, 16 .—Twice,
consistent stool (first day), 6 .—Soft'copious stool, afternoon (first day), 7 .—
* Very hard stool (second day), 6 .—Hard stool (first day); constipation (sec¬
ond day) ; at first hard and then passages of soft fteces (third day), 4 .—Hard
stool and frequent urination (tenth day), 6 .— [400.] Stool and urine de¬
layed, 6 .—No stool (third and fourth days), 6 .

Urinary Organs. —Paiuful constriction of the bladder, without
urging, 2 .—The urine only dribbles away when sitting, the bladder when in
that posture feeling bent forwards upon itself; on standing, the urine passes
freely; this lasted three or four days (after seven days), 17 .—Discharge of
yellow pus from the urethra, with redness and inflammation of the glans,
and fever in the evening, with rigors (seventh day), 7 .—Thin, powerless
stream of urine, 7 .—Pain in urethra, on waking (fourteenth night), 16 .—
* Burning while, ihe urine passes, with discharge of elongated flakes, 5 .—
Sharp cutting pains in the urethra, after some hours, 1 .—Burning with urin¬
ation, 7 . — [410.] Burning iu the whole urethra always on passing water, 1 .—
During passage of urine, scratching scraping in the whole urethra (after
twelve hours), 1 .—Desire to urinate wakes him from sleep every morning, 4 .
—Urging to urinate ceases with the perfect discharge of menses, 6 .—* Fre¬
quent desire to urinate, with scanty discharge, accompanied by burning (first
day), 6 .—Urging to urinate on appearauce of menses, 6 .—Nearly all day he
has urgent desire to urinate, but little urine passes, 1 .—Frequent urging to
urinate, with scanty but painless discharge, 6 .—Frequent desire to urinate,
discharging only a few drops, without straining, as usually before menstru¬
ation, and again at the end of menstruation (fourteenth and fifteenth days), 6 .
—When sitting in the seat after stool had a desire to urinate, but could
not; afterwards, when standing, could urinate freely, at 3.30 a.m. (seventh
day), 16 .— [420.] He has to get up two or three times in the night to urinate,
and passes a great quantity; he thinks he can never finish, at first with
burning, then without, for two weeks (after two and four days), 6 .—Frequent
urination (first day), 6 .—Frequent urination, with hard stool, 6 .—Wakes up
in the night to make water, 9 .—He urinates oftener and more than usual,
without burning (sixth day), 6 .—Without particular thirst, the uriue passes
more frequently than usual, becoming more copious daily, 4 .—Frequent co¬
pious urination (after four hours), 2 .—Abundant diuresis, 21 .—Discharge of
much watery urine, with burning in urethra (first and second days), 6 .—
Frequent discharge of pale copious urine, growing turbid on standing, like
clay-water (fifth day), 6 .— [430.] No uriue in the forenoon ; in the after¬
noon, three times in succession, discharge of pale urine, then again none, 6 .
—Passes urine but ouce during the whole day, with burning during the
discharge, but in sufficient quantity (first day), 6 .—Copious urination lessens
(sixth day), 6 .—Straining, with scanty discharge of urine (second day), 6 .—
Strangury, with pressure iu the bladder, yet the urine will not come, and
when it comes there is cutting pain, 1 .—Severe strangury, as in case of stone,
with discharge of white acrid turbid matter, with mucus, 5 .—Urine becomes


535

abundant again on the ninth day ; he has to get up nights to urinate, 6 .—
Morning urine increases in quantity to a quite unusual amount, 9 .—Pale
urine, in the afternoou ; he has to urinate frequently and passes much, 6 .—
Pale urine, voided in a thin powerless stream, with flakes in the urine, 7 .—
[440.] * Urine turbid immediately a fter its passage, like clay-ivater, and scanty
(sixth day), 6 .—Urine passes without sensation in the passage, 4 .—Urine fre¬
quently voided, does not get turbid, but deposits a cloud (seventh day), 6 .—
Urine and stool much delayed, not often and scanty (second day), 6 .— Urine
very scanty and frequently stopping, with frequent straining and burning
(fourth day), 6 .—The deep-yellow urine deposits a thin cloud (eighth day), 6 .
—Urine becomes turbid on standing, and deposits much clay-colored sedi¬
ment, for several days (after forty-eight hours), 6 .—Iridescent pellicle on the
urine, 9 .—Very fiery urine, but without burning (second day), 6 .—Red scanty
urine, mornings (fourth day), 6 .—[450.] High-colored, apparently increased
urine, during menstruation (sixteenth day), 6 .—Urine passes towards the
end mingled with blood, then with the discharge of pus, also blood, and
after this the pain when urinating abates, 7 .—The scanty urine passed,
amid frequent urging, is clear and red (first day), 6 .—Urine is turbid already
while passing, with burning (third day), 6 .

Sexual Organs. — 31ale. Intolerable odor about the genitals, 1 .—
Erections seem diminished, 6 .—Gians red and inflamed, 7 .—Tearing from
glans to root of penis, 1 .—After the passage of urine, burning and itching;
tearing pain from the glans to the root of penis, 1 .—During morning, testi¬
cles and spermatic cords ache and are tender to touch ; the cords are much
swollen, with a dragging-downwards feeling in them ; afterwards, as this
got better in the course of the morning, soreness in the left groin, worse on
touch ; in the course of the day it nearly all went off (eighth day), 16 .—
[460.] Seminal emissions at night and restless sleep, 7 .—Pollution first
night, 1 .—Painful pollution nearly every night, with lascivious dream, 7 .—
Inclination for coition several days, with frequent emissions, 7 .—Inclination
to coitus, with restless sleep, 7 .— Female* Slimy leucorrhcea rather pro¬
fuse, while walking, 6 .—Menses three days too soon (after fourteen days), 1 .
—Menses very scanty, but very acrid, with burning in the inner side of
the thighs, so that she cannot approximate them on account of pain ; the
menstrual discharge appears only now and then, 6 .—Menses three days too
late, and with every perfect discharge of menses the urging to urinate
ceases, 6 .—Appearance of menses is retarded for five days, 1 .

Respiratory Organs. — [470.] Pressing painful stitches in thyroid
cartilage, without affecting deglutition, 2 .—Hoarse all day (fourth day), 16 .
— Cough. Hard cough in the daytime, produced by a tickling ulcerative
sensation in the fauces, 1 .—Cough and headache (second day), 6 .—Cough
and coryza, 1 .—Cough, with nausea, vomiting bile, and diarrhoea, 10 *.—Cough,
without expectoration, forenoon (second day), 6 .—Dry cough, with buruing
in the nose on blowing it (fifth day), 6 .—Dry cough, excited by roughness
in the throat, only in the forenoon (second and third days), 6 .— Resjdra-
tion. Frequent deep inspirations after dinner (second day), 6 .— [480.]
Catching of breath (stoppage of breath) and oppression of the chest, in
the evening and the following morning (after forty-eight hours), 6 .—Very
asthmatic; he is often forced to breathe short (fifth day), 6 .—Difficult
breathing, 6 .—In breathing, everything too tight, 6 .— Severe catching of
breath while working; he can get air enough only with difficulty (fourth
day), 6 .—Breathing heavy and short after dinner (third day), 6 .—Stoppage
of breath, as if by spasm, or as if by an impediment in the lungs, with

536


constriction in the throat for a whole minute, accompanied with great
anxiety (after three hours), 6 .—The slightest exercise makes her short-
breathed, abating in rest, 10 *.—Shortness of breath, 6 .

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Oppression of the chest, impeding respiration, mornings (eighth
day), 6 .— [490.] Pressure in the chest, as if bruised, after attack, 1 .—Pres¬
sure in the chest, 6 .—Pressure and tightness on the chest, at night and in
the morning, without cough (eighth day), 6 .—Pressure on the chest, with
shortness of breath (sixth day), 6 .—Pressure frequently on the chest, after¬
noons (second day), 6 .—Painful constriction in the chest, alternating often
with sudden expansion (eighth day), 6 .—He feels so tight-chested, with
dyspnoea and exhaustion, that he had to loosen his necktie, lasting for some
time (seventh day), 6 . — His chest feels mostly as if screwed together, and
everything feels too tight, in breathing and walking, so that he had to
loosen his clothes, necktie, and vest, in order to get air enough, frequently
omitting and returning, 6 .—Tension across the chest after attack, 1 .—On the
outside of the chest tensive pain, as if it were too short, ou straightening
up and walking erect (after twenty-four hours), 1 .— Front and Sides.
[500.] Pressure on the sternum, worse on palpation, 3 .—Violent stinging in
the middle of sternum, mornings (third day), 6 .—Aching pain in centre of
chest; inclined to keep still in order to relieve it (after one hour), 15 .—
Stitches in the middle of the chest, beside the sternum, without affecting
respiration, 2 .—Pressing tension about the clavicle, next to sternum, 3 .—
Pressing stitches under the last true rib, 3 .—Stitches in right chest, without
affecting respiration, 2 .—Stinging in right side of chest, on motion, while
standing, afternoon, 6 . — Stinging in the right side of breast, 1 p.m. (third
day), 6 .—Stinging in the left side of chest, on walking outdoors, and in the
forehead at the same time, mornings, continuing a good while (second day), 6 .
— [510.] Stinging pain in left side of chest, while walking, 1 .—Violent
stitches in the left costal region, so that the pain doubled him up,‘in the
evening, while sitting (twelfth day), 6 .—The nipples are soft, insensible, and
not irritable, 1 .

Heart and False. —Palpitation almost constant, with some anxiety
and fearful ness, 1 .—Palpitation of the heart during the day, 10 *.—Palpitation
often in daytime, 1 . — Slight palpitation, 11 . — Pulse somewhat slower, 11 .—•
Pulse somewhat retarded, 8 .—Scarcely any alteration of pulse, unless it were
a little retarded, 19 .—[520.] Pulse fell 8 beats, but after some minutes re¬
turned to the normal, 11 .—Pulse very febrile, 11 .

Neck and Hack. — Neck. Swelling of the right side of the neck
(and throat), with pain when touched, 1 .—Wrenching pain in left side of
neck, as if in the tendon, on moving the head (second day), 6 .—Tension in
right side of neck, particularly ou moving the head, with heaviness of the.,
head, 6 .—On moving the head, tension in side of neck, pain in nape of neck,
stitches, 6 .—Tension in the nape of neck and stitches, ou moving the head
(tenth day), 6 .—In the morning pain in left side of neck, on raising head up
(tenth day), 16 .—Aching in the nape of the neck on moving the head, in the
morning, abating during the day (third day), 6 .—Chuckling or pulling in
left side of neck (second day), 6 .—[530.] Tearing in the nape of the neck,
passing thence across the vertex towards the right side of the forehead,
where it disappears, afternoon (sixth day), 6 .—Violent persistent drawing
stitches in the right cervical muscles, from the clavicle into the hyoid bone, 2 .
—In the muscles of the neck pressing stitches, increased by touch and
motion, 3 .— Hack. On deep inspiration, pain, as if something were sticking
fast to the back, 1 .—At 8 A.M., pain in muscles at inner edge of right scap-


537

ula (infraspinous portion); worse on moving either arm straight up, from
putting right arm to back or from raising it above level of shoulder, and
from rising from stooping ; pain still felt, at 8 p.M. (sixth day), 16 .—Pain in
middle of back on deep inspiration (sixth day), 16 .—Two quickly repeated
shoots about inner edge of right scapula (fifth day), 16 .—In the back, between
the shoulderblades, severe stitches, 2 .—Stinging, also tearing, beside the
spine, from the right shoulderblade to the last false rib, increased much by
inspiration, and on deep inspiration entirely arresting the breath, 3 .—Pain
in right lumbar regiou on deep inspiration, in afternoon (fifteenth dav), 16 .
— [540.] Backache in small of back, increased after protracted stooping,
pressing violently so that walking is impeded; improved by rest, when sit¬
ting or lying, but reappearing in the form of stitches with every, even the
slightest, turn of the body, abating during the afternoon (fourth day), 7 .—
Violent pain in lower part of back on stooping, and afterwards; does not
disappear during motion ; forenoon (second and third days), 6 .—*Pain in
lower part of back, passing around both sides of pelvis forward toward the
genitals; worse nights and during motion, 1 .—Pain in lower part of back
and both sides, 1 .—Stinging under the left ribs, in the lumbar region, for
two hours, regardless of respiration, 6 .—Tensive pain on the least motion,
from the sacrum across the left hip, interfering with walking, 1 .—Bruised
pain of sacral region, evenings (second day), 6 .—Crawling in sacral region
externally, like formication, in the forenoon, 6 .

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Blue nails, with coldness, 1 .—Trembling of hands and
feet, with tearing in the forehead, and pinching in abdomen, forenoon
(fourth day), 6 .— [550.] Mobility of all the limbs, 1 .—Lassitude of limbs,
dulness, stoppage of nose, 7 .—In all the joints of the body, tearing, now
here and then there, for several days, but only of short duration, 6 ,—Tear¬
ing in nearly every limb, at night, with subsequent headache (sixth day), 6 .
—Hands and feet very light, mobility, 7 .—Drawing pains in shoulderblades
and legs, 1 .

Superior Extremities. — Shoulder. Drawing in the shoulder-
blades, 1 .—Pain, as from a thrust or blow, in the shoulder, on moving the
arm ; less while at rest, 6 .—In the shoulder-joints, violent tearing, extend¬
ing gradually into the elbows, where it abates ; frequently repeated (sixth
day), 6 .—Pain in the right shoulder-joint, somewhat laming, only when
moving the arms, afternoon, until lying down, 6 .— [560.] Cracking in right
shoulder-joint, on moving it (sixteenth day), 6 .—Pain, as from a thrust or
blow, in right shoulder-joint, only on moving the arm, 6 .—Tearing in left
shoulder down into the fingers, afternoon till evening, with frequent inter¬
missions (fifth day), 6 .—Stitches in the shoulders on raising the arm (fourth
day), 6 .— Arm. In the arms, feeling of stiffness, on motion after rest; long-
continued (eighth day), 6 .—In the upper arm, near shoulder-joint, a pulse¬
like, intermittent, external, stinging paiu, 4 .—Tearing in left arm, from
shoulder to the tips of the fingers, with pressure on the chest, at 11 a.m.
(fourth day), 6 .—Violent tearing on the upper surface of left upper arm,
extending to the wrist for five minutes, with stitches in right side of chest,
at 8.30 p.m. (third dav), 6 .—Tearing in the right arm, from the shoulder-
joint to the wrist, afternoon (fourth day), 6 .—Dull stinging, above and in
front of the humerus, 3 .— Elbow and Forearm. [570.] In the elbow,
pain, as if a tendon had snapped from place, on rapid pronation of fore¬
arm, 1 .—Paralytic weariness in elbow-joints, 1 .—Twitching in both forearms, 7 .

_Pressing tearing on the ulna, sometimes extending to the metacarpal

bones, 3 .—Tearing across the forearm, above the wrist, with drawing-tearing

538


stitches towards the fingers, 2 .—About the forearms, beside the elbow-joints,
paralytic tearing; worse when at rest than in motion, 3 .—Pressing stitches
in the muscles of both ulnae, 3 .—Stinging-drawing stitches on the inside of
right forearm, 2 .—Iu afternoon, when walking in open air, stinging in radial
side of left wrist; when indoors it was not felt; afterwards when again
walking in open air, it returned (twelfth day), 16 .— JVrist. Tearing stitches
above the left wrist, upwards, 2 . —[ 580 .] Tearing in left wrist, 2 p.m. (fourth
day), 6 .—Sprained pain in right wrist, drawing toward the ring finger, 2 .—
j Hand and Fingers. Hands tremble, 6 .—Stiffness, itching, and burn¬
ing heat in the hands, with swollen veins, relieved by motion (fourteenth
day), 6 . — The hand pains without swelling, 5 . — Woke at 7 A.M., with sharp
cutting pain under thumb-nail of one hand, afterwards the other hand
(after six hours), 14 .—The thumb becomes inflamed, with throbbing and
burning; the worst at night, 1 .—Numbness of fingers, especially the third
and fourth of both hands, 12 .—Numbness (going to sleep) of the fingers, 1 .—
Pain of tips of fingers on pressure , as if ulcerated , or as if salt were put on to
a wound, \ —[ 590 .] Drawing tearing through the bones of right ring finger,
penetrating the bones; increased by motion of the joints, 2 .—On the backs
of the four fingers of the left hand, tearing towards the tips, 1.30 p.m.
(fourth day), 6 .—Pressure-like stitches in the muscles of left thumb, at rest
and in motion, 2 .—Intermittent pressing stitches in metacarpal bone of right
index finger, for two days, 3 .—Small stitches in first joint of right little
finger, 2 .—Pricking, as if caused by countless pins, in first joint of thumb ;
later, this spot aches also on being touched, 1 .

Inferior Extremities. — Unsteady gait, with vertigo, 6 . — Great
lassitude in the lower limbs; he can hardly move his legs (sixth day), 6 .—
Hip. In the hip-joints, lame, bruised, and tired ; she has to sit down, but
without relief, 1 .—On the right ischium, pressing stitches in every posture, 3 .
— Thigh. [ 600 .] Stiffness in right thigh, as if contracted, in the popli¬
teal space and calf, at the same time toes feel as if swollen under the nails
(third day), 7 .— Weariness in the thighs, during catamenia, 6 .—Pressure on
the inside of left thigh, near the knee-joint, 3 .—Dull pressure on the right
thigh, just above the popliteal region, while sitting, 2 .—Stinging pressure
about the left thigh near the patella, 3 .—Tearing pressure about the thigh,
near the knee-joint, upwards and outwards, 3 .—Sore feeling in the bend of
the right thigh, she can hardly walk ; before menstruation (fourteenth and
fifteenth days), 6 .—Violent stitches, followed by tearing in the left popliteal
space (seventh day), 6 .—On the inside of the thighs, burning; she cannot
bring them together during menstruation, 6 .—Pressing heaviness in left
thigh, while sitting or walking, without pain, 2 .— Knee . [ 610 .] Swelling
and stiffness of the knee, with stinging pain, so that he could hardly move
the knee sideways on account of pain, 1 .—On the knee single, acute, fine
stitches, on the inner side, 2 .—Weariness iu the knee-joints, the whole day, 6 .

Several painful tearings in right knee when gaping, while standing (third
day), 6 .—Tearing in left knee, 2 p.m. (fourth day), 6 .—Violent tearing about
the left knee, from evening till midnight, frequently intermitting (third
day), 6 .—Stinging tensive pressure about right knee, 2 .— Leg. More weak¬
ness and lassitude iu legs, 6 .—Cramp in the calves, at night, 1 .—Violent
cramp in the calf, 1 .— [ 620 .] Pain iu the calves, as after cramp, 1 .—Cramp
from tibia down into toes; has to try to find a position wherein it feels
easier (fourteenth day), 7 .— In the leg, tearing deep in left tibia, 3 p.m.
(eighth day), 6 .—Tearing down the right tibia, 1 p.m. (seventh day), 6 .—
Tearing iu the muscles of right lower leg, 2 .—During menses, weariness in


539

legs, 6 .—Dull drawing, upwards, above the right tibia, 2 .—When walking in
open air, stinging in left leg just above knee, anteriorly towards inner side
(seventeenth day), 16 .—Cracking in the left ankle-joint, on every motion
(fifth day), 6 .— Foot <nul Toes. Swelling of the feet, 1 .—[630.] Swelling
and redness of the right tarsus, with pain, increased in the afternoon, 5 .—
Swollen feeling in both feet, with itching and heat in the soles, relieved
after some exercise (fourteenth day), 6 .—Constantly tired in the feet, when
standing, for several days, 6 .—Painful drawing changed into twitching, on
the dorsum of right foot, 2 .—The soles of the feet are painfully sensitive, 1 .—
Violent tearing in left sole, after midnight, from the heel towards the toes ;
then violent itching; and after scratching, a hard stitch through the heel,
extending into dorsum of foot (eighth day), 6 .—Tensive feeling in the right
foot, as if it were swollen, 1 .—Painful throbbing, pressing, and pricking on
the inside of right sole, and then on the whole sole, while sitting, 2 .—His
toes ache about the nails, as if swollen, 7 .—Tensive feeling in the tendons
and in the toes of the left foot, as if the toes were being violently drawn,
inwards, lasting one hour, slowly abating, morning (fifth day), 6 .—[640.]
Tearing and drawing in the great toe of the right foot, 2 .—Tearing in the
left great toe, more towards the tip, evenings (fifth day), 6 .

Generalities. —No exertion seemed to tire, 12 .—Feeling of strength, 6 .—
The whole body has a greater mobility ; hands and feet feel very light
the first days, 7 .—Suddenly fell backwards on the floor, 1 .—In the whole
body, trembling with anxiety, 1 .—Attack of nausea after breakfast, with
sour eructation ; while standing by the open window he becomes dizzy, he
lost his consciousness, fell backwards to the floor, and after being raised,
he came to himself, and felt great tension across the chest, 1 .—So weak that
she can hardly walk, 106 .—^General weakness, 11 .—[650.] ^Sensation of weak¬
ness over the whole body, 11 .—Great prostration of strength, a degree of
torpor, which induced him to lie upon the ground, with unwillingness to
move or get up, 19 .—Weary in his legs, he feels as if he would have a spell
of sickness, forenoon (second day), 6 .—Great weariness, particularly in the
legs, but principally in the thighs, knees, and feet, also during menses, 6 .—
Lassitude and tired feeling in the whole body, in the forenoon, passing off
after the meal, 6 .—Lightning-like tensive pains, here and there, in the body,
and about the head, 1 .—Racking effects, 18 .— During the stool, in the even¬
ing, faintness, 1 .—Vinegar seems to aggravate the complaints at first, 1 .—
Out of doors, seems better, 6 .—[660.] To smell camphor, antidotes, 1 .

Skill. — Objective. Many little warts, 1 . — Tetters appear on all parts
of the body, 1 .—Pale red, slightly elevated, rough spots upon the forehead,
of the size of a split pea, without itching, 7 .—Itching humor on forehead,
burning and moist after rubbing it, three days before the menses, 1 .—A scab
on lobule of ear, first with burning pain, then itching, 1 .—Itching eruption
under the nose, 1 .—Itching eruption under the nose, as if caused by an acrid
discharge, 1 .—Eruption in left nostril; sore nose, 1 .—Tetter upon the upper
lip, with pains, as of many pins, 1 .—[670.] Nettlerash eruption like urticaria,
itching intolerably, and stinging on the neck, chest, eyelids, hands, and
the whole body, with violent burning after rubbing, 1 .—Tetters on the
hands, 1 .—Herpes on prepuce, 1 .—Red herpetic spots on the calves, with
severe itching, 1 .—Several great cracks in the skin of the right thumb, “so
that one can see the flesh,” with burning pain (sixth day), 6 .—Rashlike
pimples, as soon as he comes into the cold air from the warm room, 1 .—A
child, twenty months old, had what appeared to be a simple case of herpes
lahiales, which had broken out six weeks before; it consisted of two small

540


irregular shaped patches half an inch or more in diameter, commencing
beneath the labial commissure, and extending towards the mesial line of
the chin ; the crusts were thick, of a dirty yellowish-brown color, surrounded
by an inflamed areola and suppurating border; I prescribed for my patient;
when she returned at the expiration of two weeks, the patches had united
in the centre, and extending downwards covered the entire chin, while sur¬
rounding its borders was an occasional pustule, denoting the invasion of
the cheeks; the mother now informed me that the left hip was involved,
and an examination of the part disclosed several patches and pustules
extending from the anterior superior spine in an oblique direction, upwards
and backwards towards the lumbar region ; the characteristic crusts had
become detached by contact with the clothing, and in consequence it pre¬
sented an angry and inflamed appearance, not at all unlike a well-defined
case of herpes zoster; the new crop which was being developed, began by
small pustules on an inflamed base, some of the size of a pin-head, others
as large as a common pea, single and discrete at first, but as they ap¬
proached each other, or where they were more numerous, inclining to be¬
come confluent; the least abrasion of the cuticle was transformed into a
suppurating pustule. I prescribed Graphites, Hepar, Arsenicum, Merc,
sol., and Mezereum, in various dilutions, from the 3d to 30th, and 200th
potencies, for about two months, without the least apparent benefit; the
eruption had now covered both cheeks, and several pustules on the nose,
forehead, and neck foreshadowed its onward march, while the patch on the
hip had extended to the spinal column ; the itching was very troublesome
and persistent, and the child’s sleep much disturbed in consequence. The
eldest boy (about twelve) had a well-defined case of herpes phlyctenodes,
as large as the palm of the hand, on the left side of the neck, from the ear
in front to the spiue behind, and extending from the hairy scalp down the
neck about three inches. The other two children had small irregular
patches ou the face and left arm ; and wherever the skin was abraded on
the hands suppurating pustules were to be seen. I gave the three youngest
a few doses of Camphor, and in a week the whole trouble had disappeared.
I allowed the oldest boy to recover by the natural process of the drug, and
the neck is not yet clear of the crusts, but there has been no increase of
the symptoms since discontinuing the Sarsaparilla, 13 .—Larger and smaller
pimples in face not painful, 10 *.—Itching pimple® on the cheek, inflamed far
around, with violent burning, resulting in a thick large scab, and causing
a tearing-burning pain in the open air (after nineteen days), 1 .—Smaller
and larger pimples or boils in the face, mostly on the cheeks, 108 .—[680.]
A suppurating pimple on right side of nose (eighth day), 6 .—This morning
found a pimple, painful to touch, on left zygoma (thirteenth day), 16 .—Itch¬
ing pimples ou the chin (tenth day), 6 .—Violent itching on chin ; after it,
several very small pimples (twenty-first day), 6 .—Eruption of pimples on
the sides of the chin, with itching, soon containing pus in their apices, 1 .—
Unbearable itching on scrotum and perinseum; after scratching, little pim¬
ples rise, oozing a moisture, and keep the part sore (several cases), 108 .—Red
pimples of the size of a pin head, without moisture, on the back and thighs;
only in warmth it is (corroding) itching, which vanishes only for a short
time after scratching, 3 .—On the ends of the fingers, runuing-around ulcera¬
tions, always after using Sarsaparilla in the autumn, 10 *.—Violent itching on
both thighs, after scratching many pimples rise, soon disappearing again
(fifth day), 6 .—Pimples on the fingers, 10 *.—[690.] Itching and many red
pimples over the right knee; the pimples are still out next day, but do not


541

itch (seventh day), 6 .—The right index inflamed around the nail, like a
run-around; later the same on the left, 10 ®.—Itching on the right calf, then
many pimples rise, evening, 6 .—Limpid vesicle on the right side of under
lip (fourth day), 6 .—An itching little blister under the chin (fourth day), 6 .—
Itching with vesicles, or with pimples after scratching, on the forearms,
thighs, knees, calves, and other places, 6 .—Itching on the inside of the right
forearm; after scratching, two blisters rose, soon disappearing again, 6 .—
Large clear vesicle on the inner side of the right wrist, behind the little
finger, first itching, then burning; after opening the blister, discharge of
watery fluid, increased burning, inflammation, and a scab, itching par¬
ticularly in the night, 6 .—Violent itching on the outside and front surface
of the left thigh ; after scratching, a great many little blisters appear, but
soon are gone again, afternoou, 6 .—Violent itching in the hollow of the
knees; after long scratching, many little blisters come up, soon going away
again, afternoons and mornings, 6 . — [700.] Pustules which have been
scratched open leave ulcers suppurating for a long time, 6 .—Pustule in the
middle of forehead, remaining several days (eighth day), 6 .—Pustules on
the face, without sensation, 3 .—Small pustules on the right side of nose, on
the right dorsal side of toot, left gluteal region, sometimes with stinging
pain on touch, 6 .—Itching pustules on the fingers and other parts of the
body (after nine days), 1 .—Two small pustules on the dorsum of right foot
(eighth day), 6 .—Furuncle on the left buttock, stinging when touched, last¬
ing three days (after twenty-two days), 6 . — Subjective. Formication in
the left foot, on raising it and putting it down, 5 p.m., 6 . —Pricking from
within outwards, in skin in the face, most about the neck, 3 .—Pricking from
within outwards, most and strongest about the neck, with heat on chest,
back, and face, 3 .—[710.] Pricking, as if caused by needles, over the ex¬
ternal malleolus of the right foot, 3 .—Pricking itching over the whole body,
evenings, from 5 to 7 o’clock, and in the morning on rising, 1 .—Fine prick¬
ing itching in face and scalp, as well as about the neck and shoulders, with
feeling of great warmth in these parts; on scratching, it begins at once in
another place, 2 .—Pricking and itching about neck and shoulders with heat;
on scratching, it begins at once in another place, 2 .—Burning itching over
the whole body, with rigors, 1 .—Burning itching on the abdomen, over the
thighs, 1 .—Itching on many places, or nearly every part of the body, at
various times, even on the scalp and face; scarcely relieved by scratching,
or returning afterwards, 6 .—Itching on the whole body, here and there,
most severe in the evening, before and after lying down; very much aggra¬
vated by scratching, 6 .—Itching all over, night, does not let him fall asleep
(fifth day), 6 .—Itching every night before going to sleep, passing off in bed, 1 .
—[720.] Itching here and there about the body, scratching does not relieve
it long (fifth day), 6 .—Itching on the whole body, before and after lying
down ; the more he scratches the more he itches, 6 .—Itching, now iu the
right, then in the left lobule, later in the nape of neck, thighs, etc. (fourth
day), 6 .—Itching in left ear, not stopped by scratching (eighth day), 6 .—
Violent itching in left external meatus, in the morning, 6 o’clock, not to
be stopped by scratching, 6 .—Itching on the whole forehead; after scratch¬
ing, still returning (eighth day), 6 .—Itching on the whole face, not lessened
bv & scratching (fourth day), 6 .—Itching on right wing of nose, scratching
does not stop it (ninth day), 6 .—Itching on the left side of the nose and
around the eyes, 1 .—Itching externally on abdomen, disappearing after
scratching, evening, 6 .—[730.] Itching around the navel does not cease after
scratching’ returning frequently, 6 .—Itching in the right flank, disappears

542


after scratching, 6 .—Itching about the nipples, 1 .—Itching on the back the
whole afternoon ; not much relieved by scratching (fourth day), 6 . Itching
ou the forearm, towards the hand, and on the inside of the knee, above the
hollow of the knee, particularly evenings in bed, 1 .—Itching on the hand
and backs of fingers, 1 .—Itching in front of wrist, not ceasing after scratch¬
ing, forenoon (ninth day), 6 .—Itching on the right hip, will not abate by
scratching, 6 .—Severe itching on both hip-bones, disappears after scratching,
forenoon (ninth day), 6 .—Itching on the right buttock, disappears from
scratching, but soon returns, evenings, 6 .—[740.] Itching on the thigh above
the left knee; it abates after scratching, but returns again and again, after¬
noon (fifth day), 6 .—Itching, with burning after scratching, below the calves,
in the evening and morning, 6 .—Violent itching on the tendon below the
calves, where it burns after scratching, evening and morning (fifth day), 6 .
—Pricking like pins in the calves, 10 *.—Violent itching under both knee-
joints, and in front above the knees; has to scratch, which does not relieve
it entirely (third day), 6 .—Itching on the external edge of the right foot;
on the ankle he has to scratch until it bleeds, evening (second day), 6 .—
Itching on top of right foot; after scratching, it goes on the left tibia,
where it finally disappears, after repeated scratching, afternoon, 6 .—Itching
and drawing in the sole, 1 .

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Frequent gaping; fills his eyes full of water (first day), 6 .—
Constant gaping, 1 .—[750.] Frequent gaping, with crawlings, the whole
forenoon (eighth day), 6 . — Drowsy, 18 .—Sleepiness and internal chill, 1 .—
Sleepiness, with gaping (very soon), 1 .—Very sleepy and sluggish, forenoon,
without being much indisposed, 6 .—Soon falls asleep, in the evening, with
violent starting (eighth day), 6 .—Falls asleep, in the evening; startling
dreams of falling, slipping with the feet, etc.; frightful startling (eighth
day), 6 .—At night and in the morning, on waking, finds himself lying on
his back, every night, 1 .—Woke on back and found there had been an
emission, but without dreams (twentieth and twenty-second days), 16 .—Woke
on back (twelfth and subsequent nights), 16 .—[760.] Woke on back, sleep¬
ing later than usual (thirteenth day), 16 .—After midnight awaking several
nights at 2 o’clock, and then remains awake for a long time (eighth day), 6 .
—Waking after midnight with cutting pains in the abdomen ; in the morning
the pains cease (second day), 6 .—She wakes partially at night on account of
pain, without knowing where, hut in the morning she thought it must have
been in her abdomen (one day before menses), (fourteenth day), 6 .—Waking
at night out of voluptuous dreams, without erection (second day), 6 .— Waking
at night, as if frightened by a sound,*.—Five times-starting up at night in
a fright, and thereupon difficulty of falling asleep again (second day), 6 .—
At night she started up, hurriedly scratched her thigh unconsciously above
the knee, and then slept again immediately (fourth day), 6 .—Little sleep, with
starting up (sixth day), 6 .—An almost sleepless night, without an apparent
cause, 6 .—[770.] Restless sleep, with much turning, 1 .—Sleep much inter¬
rupted (tenth day), 6 .—Restless unrefreshing sleeo, 1 .—Restless sleep, with
dreams of disaster, 1 .—Restless sleep at night, with inclination to coitus;
seminal emissions and twitching in both forearms, 7 .—Iu the hours before
midnight he cannot sleep, owing to restlessness in his whole body and soul,
and an uncommon mobility iu all the limbs, 1 .—Dreamed of urgent desire
for stool, with severe aching in anus; woke and found it a reality, at 3.30
a.m. (seventh day), 16 . — Dreams. Unpleasant dreams (twelfth night) ;
amorous dreams, with erection and copious seminal emission ; afterwards
dream without emission (fourteenth night); amorous dreams when lying


543

on right side, with emission (twenty-sixth night) ; amorous dream ; always
afterwards woke on back (thirty-fourth day), 16 .—He dreams, towards morn¬
ing, several white spectres came into his room and near his bed ; he was at
first shocked and very much frightened, but recovered himself, and struck
them down with both his fists, so that they all fell to the ground ; after
which his nose bled, and it woke him, and he thought he had struck him¬
self on his nose (third day), 6 .—He saw in his dream several long ago-de¬
ceased relations (twelfth day), 6 .—[780.] Heavy dreams, full of frights, but
cannot recollect what (fifth and sixth days), 6 .—Dreams of the business of
the day before (sixth day), 6 .—Dreams she is sleigh-riding and the sleigh
upsets; she starts violently and wakens up (eighth day), 6 . — Lascivious
dreams, without erections (second and tenth days), 6 .—Dreams of horrible
things, for iustauce, a big spider, 1 .—Horrible dreams in a deep sleep, 1 .—
Dreams of vexation, 6 .—Dreams of what was talked about the day before
(second day), 6 .

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Ch illiness. Violent chill before dinner, with shaking and
chattering of teeth, for oue-quarter of an hour; abates after “ wasser soup”
(first day), 6 .—Chilly rigor, evenings, on lying down, passing off in bed
(second day), 6 .—[790.] Gaping, chills, with shaking, inward coldness and
external heat, or both mixed, thirst, coughing, and vomiting, 10 *.—Coldness
on awaking, at night, 6 .—Chilly, in afternoon (fifth day), 16 .—Chill, at night,
on waking (ninth day), 6 .—Shaking chill, at night, without subsequent heat
(fifth day), 6 . — Chill, in the morning, in bed, for a quarter of an hour
(eighth day), 6 .—Chills and shaking without external coldness, 6 .—Inclined
to chills and rigors, a short time in the forenoon, then, till evening, warmth,
with sweat, over whole body, 6 .—Chill and coldness over whole body, even
near the stove, with unusual warmth of the face and chest, 3 .—Rigors, with
burning itching, 1 .—[800.] Feverish coldness, frequent in the day, with blue
nails and loss of all vital warmth in arms and legs, 1 .—Chilliness, even in
the warm room (second day), 6 .—He can warm himself but with difficulty
in the warm room, all the forenoon (second day), 6 .—Rigor over the whole
body, from below upwards?. —Overrun by transient chills, in the forenoon, 6 .
—Chill runs over her as soon as she gets into the open air (eighth day), 6 .
—Internal chill and sleepiness, 1 .—In the evening chill for one hour, with¬
out subsequent heat or sweat (seventh day), 6 .—Frequently wakes up at
night with coldness (second day), 6 .—Severe chill at night in bed, with very
cold feet, accompanied by heat of face and chest, 3 .—[810.] Shuddering,
with gooseflesh, accompanied by continual eructation, in the forenoon
(eighth day), 6 .—He shudders from stitches in head, 2 .—Chills frequently
on the arms, thighs, back, and on inside of abdomen, 1 .—Cold hands, colder
towards the tips of the fingers, for eight days, 4 .—Coldness of the feet, 1 .—
Heat. Heat, evenings, in bed, an hour before falling asleep; the blood
boils, the heart beats, and sweat stands on the forehead, for two successive
evenings. 1 . — Heat in the whole body for a short time, 10 a.m., 6 . —Increased
warmth, merriment, and feeling of strength, in the evening (ninth day), 6 .—
Very warm in the whole body, as if sweat were to break out, after break¬
fast (eighth day), 6 .—General warmth, with thirst, even in the morning,
and continuing all day, 6 .—[820.] The whole body seems to be in a con¬
stant febrile condition, 1 .—Fever, in the evening, with rigors, 7 .—Very warm
in the head during dinner, with sweat on the forehead (second day), 6 .—
Heat of the face, of short duration, with frontal sweat, and with heat on
the chest and back, combined with pricking from within outwards, most
and strongest about the neck, 3 .—Heat in the face, 1 .—Great warmth in face,

544


scalp, neck, shoulders, with prickling, 2 .—Unusual warmth of face, 23 .—
Unusual warmth of chest, heat, 3 .— Sweat. Profuse perspiration, 11 .—At
night, on waking, much sweating on the joints, 1 .—[830.] Severe nightsweat
after attack, 1 .— Sweat on forehead* 6 ; stands on forehead, evening, in bed, 1 .
—Frontal sweat, 3 .—Much sweat of the hands, 1 .

Conditions. —Aggravation. — (Morning), Vertigo and nausea; all
objects affect eyes ; burning and agglutination of lids ; tearing in right ear;
sneezing and running coryza; on waking, tongue rough ; dry mouth ; bitter
taste in mouth ; sour slimy taste; mucus in throat; roughness and hoarse¬
ness in throat; nausea; desire to urinate; oppression of chest; stinging in
middle of sternum ; on walking outdoors, stinging in left side of chest and
in forehead ; prickling itching over whole body.— (Forenoon), Inclined to
weep and out of humor; anxiety; head stupid and dull; dry cough;
crawling in sacral region.— (Afternoon), Ill-tempered ; moody; inclined to
work; belching of sour water; on motion, stinging in right side of chest;
swelling and redness of right tarsus, with pain.— (Evening), Stitches in left
frontal protuberance; tearing behind left ear; belching of bitter sour water;
fluid stools; swelling and redness of right tarsus, with pain ; tearing in left
great toe; 5 to 7 p.m., pricking itching over whole body ; itching; in bed,
heat.— (Night), Before midnight, soul and body restless; headache; pollu¬
tion; pain in lower part of back ; throbbing and burning in thumbs; cramp
in calves.— (Blowing nose), Burning in it.— (Cold draught of air). Tearing
in teeth.— (Cold drinks), Tearing in teeth.— (Coming from cold air into
ivarm room), Rashlike pimples.—( Closing eyes), Stinging in them.— (Every
other day), Lachrymation of eyes; hoarseness in throat.—( When gaping),
Tearing in left knee.— (Gazing long at one object), Vertigo.— (Inspiration),
Tearing from right shoulder to last false rib.— (Deep inspiration), Pressure
in left side of abdomen; pain in back; pain in right lumbar region.—
(Daring meals), Absence of thirst.— (Daring menses), Griping in pit of
stomach; weariness in thighs; burning on inside of thighs.— (Motion),
Pressure in head ; pain in lower part of back.— (Moving neck), Pain in
nape of neck.— (Moving shoulder-joint), Cracking in it.— (Moving arm),
Pain in muscles of right scapula; pain in shoulders. — ( Raising arm),
Stitches in the shoulders.— (Reading by candlelight), Pain in eyes.— (Daring
rest), Tearing about forearms.— (Scratching), Itching.—( While sitting), Ver¬
tigo ; pressure on right thigh ; heaviness in left thigh ; throbbing, pressing,
and pinching on right foot.—(After long sitting), Dulness of the head, etc.—
(Smoking), Pain in lower gums.—( When standing), Tired feeling in feet.—
(Stooping), Pain in lower part of back.— (After stooping), Backache.—
( Talking), Rending in brain.— (Touch), Pains about head; pain about tem¬
poral bone; pain in epigastrium. —(Turning eyes to left), Bam in left eye.—
(While urinating), Burning in urethra.— (Vinegar), Complaints.—( Walk-
ing), Vertigo; pressure in head; rending deep in brain; pain about head;
stinging pain in left side of chest; heaviness in left thigh.— (Walking in
open air), Throbbing in frontal region ; stinging in left wrist; stinging in
left leg.

Amelioration. —( Toward evening), Dulness of head.—( Out of doors),
Stinging in forehead; stinging in eyes; seems better.— (After exercise).
Swollen feeling in both feet.— (Motion), Stiffness, etc., in hands.— (Rest),
Backache.— (Smelling camphor), The symptoms.— (Touch), Stitches at root
of right mastoid process.

iting of a pale-yellow glairy matter, which continued at short intervals

SCORPIO.

Scorpio (species various).

Animal kingdom. Class, Arachnida. Order, Scorpiodia.

Authorities. 1 , All. Horn. Zeit, 15, 63, symptoms quoted from the French ;
2, Morisson, Gaz. des Hop., 1863, No. 61, from Bull, de Med. de Norde de
France, effects of sting; 3, Skelton, Observator Medico (of the City of
Mexico) Med. Record, 1877, 12, p. 370, effects of sting.

The bitten part very much swollen, with violent pains, lasting from one
to three days, 1 .—When an individual has been stung the symptoms may be
grouped in three distinct periods: in the first there is heat and pain at the
injured spot, general sleepiness, frequent sneezing, restlessness, aud slight
strabismus; in the second stage saliva is abundantly secreted, there is me-
teorism, dilatation of the pupil, and pulse varying between 100 and 120 ;
in the third stage there is trismus or tetanus; the first period occurs soon
after the sting, and lasts from a quarter of an hour to an hour; the sec¬
ond a little more than fifteen minutes; and the third may be prolonged
to three days. Among the native Indians cases are very frequent, and
many of the children die ; in all children under four years of age the sting
is usually fatal; between six and ten severe, but not mortal, while adults
never die. Many persons claim to have been stung without experiencing
any symptoms; this, in Dr. Puerte’s opinion, is because the clothing has
absorbed the virus, a fact he seems to have proved experimentally. When
the naked skin receives the virus symptoms of poisoning are sure to follow, 3 .—
Complete prostration so that the patient could no longer go about, 1 .—Al¬
ways acute pains and diminished temperature of part bitten, 2 .

Mead. —Vertigo in the top of the head, while standing (after two
hours), 1 .—Vertigo, with severe aching in the supraorbital region, 2 .—
Dizziness, fulness, and pressure in the vertex, 2 .—Heaviness and dulness iu

pally in the occiput and vertex, causing a congested state of the conjunctiva,
with puffiness, 2 .—Fulness of the head, with vertigo, 2 .—Darting pain at the

darting to the right eye, 2 .—[10.] Headache above the eyebrows, while
walking (after three hours), 1 .—Frontal headache in the morning, 1 .—
Slight pressure in the forehead, at 7 a.m., 1 . —A severe headache through
the temples, appearing every morning, extending to the vertex and occi¬
put, 2 .—Pain iu the left temple, 2 .—Severe lancinating pain in the vertex,
forehead, and temples; dull and throbbing, returning periodically; worse
on resting, or being in the open air, also when leaning forwards, or ap¬
plying oneself to study, 2 .

Eye. —Cutting pains, with great pain, in the eyes, causing me to al¬
most lose the power of moving them, which after a few hours passed off after
a profuse perspiration, 2 .—Pulsating stitches in the right eyebrow, 1 .—Sore¬
ness of the eyeballs, 1 .—Black spots, etc., before the eyes ; afterwards a film
appeared to come over the eyes, in the evening, 2 .—Upon closing the eyes
objects would make their appearance, 2 .

Ear. — [20.] Ringing in the ears and sudden loss of hearing (after four
hours and a half), 1 .

sections.label: Nose
sections.text: Dry coryza, with sternutation, 2 .

sections.label: Face
sections.text: Pleasant warmth in the cheeks, 1 .

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Teeth feel as if they were loose, with pain in carious teeth,
worse iu upper thau in lower jaw, 2 .—Gums bleed very freely, 2 .—Mouth
dry after the first day ; “the first day great increase in the flow of saliva,”
great thirst, and a constant effort at deglutition, 2 .—Accumulation of water
in a small spot on the tip of the tongue, which was sweetish, 1 .—A qualmish
sticky taste just above the pit of the throat, frequently lasting an hour,
with a sensation as if a soft substance (a plug of mucus) were lodged there, 1 .
—Bitter taste in mouth, 2 .

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Thick, tenacious, offensive mucus iu the throat, in the fore¬
noon, 1 .—[30.] Rancid taste in the throat, with great weakness and stiffness
in the hollows of the knees, 1 .—Irritation of the oesophagus, 2 .

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Great increase of appetite duriug the first days, but after¬
wards correspondingly less, with nausea, lasting for several days, with a
weakness and oppression in the epigastric region, 2 .—Feeling in the stom¬
ach as if a person had been fasting or missed his regular mealtime, 2 .—
(Was troubled with dyspepsia, which has disappeared up to the present
time, one month after), 2 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Pain in right hypochondrium, worse on taking a deep in¬
spiration, or lying on that side, 2 .—Twisting-pinching pain in the umbilicus
(left side), 2 .—Colic just below the navel and some griping in the side, in
the afternoon, 1 .—Severe colic, 2 .—Griping in the forepart of the abdomen,
below the navel, at 7 a.m. (after a slight vexation), 1 .—[40.] Pain in sig-

moid flexure, 2 .—Dull heavy periodic paiu, worse when the abdomen is com¬
pressed, legs extended, 2 .

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Several stools per day, with tenesmus*?.

Urinary Organs. —Pinching and tearing as if in the left ureter,
extending from the anterior superior spine of the ilium dowu to the pubis, 1 .
—Increased secretion of urine, with burning in the urethra, 2 .—Frequent
scanty emission of urine, in the afternoon, 1 .

Respiratory Organs .—Upon turning on either side violent dysp¬
noea, worse on the right than left, with cutting in the liver on pressure, 2 .—

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Oppression of the chest, with a tremulous movemeut, as from
much weeping, 1 .—Pain in the whole of the right lung, on taking a deep in¬
spiration, which causes cough, without expectoration, 2 .—Cutting pain in the
superior part of the left lung, increased by breathing the cold air, 2 .— [50.]
A feeling of constriction ot the chest, making one feel very uneasy, 2 .—
—Cramplike pain transversely across the lower part of the chest, as after
much weeping (after four hours), 1 .—Pain about the bifurcation of the tra¬
chea, 2 .—Slight pain in chest, with accelerated inspiration, 2 .—Severe stitches
in the right side, about the sixth rib, with shivering and slight irritation of
the bronchia, and general lassitude, 2 .—Violent pinching stitches in the vi¬
cinity of the last true ribs of the right side, while walking, during rest,
seeming to be in the liver (after ten hours) ; repeated half an hour later, 1 .
—The chest symptoms were all removed by a dose of Bry, 2 .

Heart and Raise. —A peculiar sense of anguish in the prsecordise,
worse after taking food, 2 .—An indescribable sensation in the region of the
heart, with severe palpitation, beating so loud that it could be heard at the
distance of several feet, 2 .—Pulse very full, but regular, ranging from 65
to 100, during the proving, 2 .

Neck and Hack. —[60.] Stiffness of the neck, with pain and con¬
traction of the right sterno-cleido-mastoid muscle, 2 .—Pain in the whole
spinal column, with slight opisthotonos, 2 .—Pain in the small of the back, 2 .

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
A drawing rheumatic pain in all the flexor muscles
of the arms and legs, 2 .—Tingling in the extremities, like one having struck
or compressed a nerve, 2 .

Superior Extremities.— Deepseated cutting pain in all the mus¬
cles of the arms, 2 .—Tingling of the arms and hands (after half an hour), 1 .
—Sticking and drawing in the palm of the right hand, from the joints of
the fingers to the middle of the hand, as far as the carpal bones (a kind of
muscular cramp in the palms, at 4 p.m.), 1 .

Generalities. —Great bodily weakness, being almost unable to walk
a short distance, 2 . A very disagreeable feeling of languor and nervous
prostration, with inclination to lie down and rest, 2 .—[70.] Muscular debility,
etc.,. Cutting pain in the articulations, similar to Rhus, but more intense,
lasting much longer, aggravated by rest in the open air, and relieved by
being in a warm room; darting from the knee and ankle joints, which feel
stiff,'.—The symptoms are worse on right side, and aggravated by rest in
open air, and relieved in a warm room, 2 .

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
Sallow condition of skin, 2 .—Burning all over the surface when
rubbed, 2 . Prickly itching all over the surface, similar to fleabites; with¬
out any change of color or rising of vesicles, worse on the back of the hand
and on the inside of the wrists, also between the fingers, 2 .

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Great sleepiness, weariness, and fulness in the whole body, in
the forenoon, 1 .—Overpowering disposition to sleep and long sleep, in the

ness, after rising in the morning, for several hours, passing off with a pro¬
